about.title: About HamPrep
about.subtitle: Your companion for Foundation licence exam preparation.
about.examFormat: The Foundation exam consists of 26 multiple-choice questions covering all syllabus topics (Betts, 2019).
about.aboutSite: HamPrep is a free study tool to help you prepare for the UK Foundation Amateur Radio licence exam. Practice with topic quizzes and full mock exams to build your confidence.
about.disclaimer: This site is not affiliated with Ofcom or the RSGB. Always refer to the official syllabus for the most up-to-date exam content.
about.howToIntro: The Foundation exam is run by the RSGB (Radio Society of Great Britain) on behalf of Ofcom (Ofcom, 2024). You can sit it from home online or in person at a local club or exam centre (RSGB, 2024).
about.howToOnline: You can take the exam at home via a video call with an RSGB-approved invigilator. You need a webcam, microphone, and a stable internet connection. Book through the RSGB website.
about.howToInPerson: Many local amateur radio clubs run exam sessions. Find a club near you through the RSGB Club Finder. Exams are typically held on evenings or weekends.
about.howToBook: Visit the RSGB exams page to register and book your exam slot. The fee is around £27.50 (RSGB, 2024). You will receive your result within a few days, and your callsign and licence from Ofcom shortly after.
about.howToWhatYouNeed: You just need a form of photo ID. A band plan, frequency chart, and licence schedule are provided during the exam — you do not need to memorise them.
about.tierIntro: UK amateur radio has three licence levels (Ofcom, 2024). Each tier unlocks more power and more frequency bands. You must pass each level in order.
about.tierFoundationDesc: Entry level — 10 watts max (Betts, 2019). Covers the basics of radio, safety, and licensing. This is the exam HamPrep helps you prepare for.
about.tierIntermediateDesc: 50 watts max and access to more bands (Ofcom, 2024). Requires a practical assessment and a harder theory exam. You must hold a Foundation licence first.
about.tierFullDesc: 400 watts max and access to all amateur bands (Ofcom, 2024). The most advanced theory exam. You must hold an Intermediate licence first.
about.tierAfterPassing: After passing your Foundation exam, you receive a callsign (e.g. M7ABC) and can start transmitting straight away. Many people progress through all three tiers over a few months to a year.
